newsitem.title: UK: Redland makes cautious trading statement.
newsitem.headline: Redland makes cautious trading statement.

text.p: Redland Plc said on Wednesday that fourth quarter volumes in Continental Europe, excluding German roofing, are slightly behind expectations.
It also said that the decision to delay the introduction of a major new Braas accessory product and a slower than expected improvement in German margins was affecting the level of profitability.
Chairman, Rudolph Agnew, also told the company's annual meeting that the strength of sterling was having an adverse impact on the translation of foreign earnings.
British-based building products group Redland said that agreement has now been signed for the reorganisation of its European roofing business and our 50.76 per cent owned German subsidiary Braas.
Redland said earlier this month that the reorganisation would result in a cash payment of 220 million stg from Braas.
By 1416 GMT, shares in Redland had tumbled 27p to stand at 368-1/2p.
